doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

chapter: Europe, expatriates and The Loud Minority
title: Expatriate musicians and Upstate New York talent
summary: Foster lists musicians who moved to Europe, then the group trades Upstate New York names.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That right. Ben Webster, Don Byas, Coleman Hawkins. Now some have come back, you know Slide Hampton lived over there for years. I think Johnny Griffin still lives over there.
Art Farmer, as far as I know, is still a resident of Vienna, but I don’t know if he came back or not. And there are some others like —

Ed Thigpen, yes, and of course Kenny Clarke, the late Kenny Clarke, the late Leo Wright who played with Dizzy, and there were some great musicians who got jobs in the studio. Herb Geller, an alto saxophonist, white American, he went over there and so did Sal Nistico.
Bad Upstate New Yorkers, boy. There’s some energy around here.
That has persisted down through the –
Nick Brignola, Sammy Noto, of course the Mangione brothers.
Steve Gadd, yeah, around the Utica-Schenectady-Syracuse-Rochester area, a whole lot of special energy going on. And them paisanos.
